name: get_type_attr_as_size
reason: getTypeAttrAsSize/asSsize mirror the 3.15.2 body (:30-41: the lookup's own error, the new PyErr_Occurred branch, the "Missed attribute" TypeError, then PyLong_AsSsize_t's non-int TypeError and OverflowError, Objects/longobject.c:708-751 checked) and sizeOrNull is the callers' n < 0 test; SizeReadSpec pins every content of the dict, the negative int returning -1 with nothing set is refuted with a bug record reproducing on 3.15.2 and main, and honest_reads feeds the exact specs of New, the constructor, reduce and replace.

name: get_real_size
reason: realSize is Py_SIZE + (tp_basicsize - 32) / 8; the Nat subtraction matches the signed C because every type that finishes construction has tp_basicsize >= 32 (check_basicsize_includes_size_and_offsets, typeobject.c:5207-5212, for NewType); NewIndexContract pins realSize = n on the honest layout, ReduceSpecC and ReplaceSpecC use it for their loop bounds, and NewTypeBasicsizeExact records the one built type (2^29 hidden fields) whose tp_basicsize makes it undercount.

name: PyStructSequence_New
reason: pssNew reads n_fields then n_sequence_fields, allocates through gcNewVar (the size_t wrap and rounding of _PyObject_VAR_SIZE, Include/cpython/objimpl.h:22-26, and gc_alloc's PY_SSIZE_T_MAX - presize refusal, Python/gc.c:2012-2028), resets the hash word, sets Py_SIZE and NULLs n_fields slots; NewIndexContract pins both allocator outcomes and the exact block on every honest type, NewReadsFirst pins that a failing read decides the result before any allocation, and the NULL-without-exception path is refuted with a bug record.

name: PyStructSequence_SetItem
reason: pssSetItem is the release-build store with the asserts compiled out; NewIndexContract proves that on a fresh honest object every documented index 0 <= i < n_fields is written alone (read back, every other index unchanged) and that i < 0 or past the block is undefined behaviour, which a constant or neighbour-clobbering SetItem would fail.

name: PyStructSequence_GetItem
reason: pssGetItem is the unchecked borrowed read of a release build; NewIndexContract pins it to return exactly what SetItem stored at every documented index and undefined behaviour outside the block, and ReprShape uses it for the item reads of structseq_repr.

name: structseq_traverse
reason: The no-behaviour reason applies under the stated GC traversal policy: the body visits the heap type and the get_real_size items and returns 0.

name: structseq_dealloc
reason: The no-behaviour reason applies under the stated tp_dealloc policy: it untracks, XDECREFs the get_real_size items (gh-122527 comment checked), frees the block and DECREFs a heap type; it calls no PyObject_ClearWeakRefs (a field named __weaklistoffset__ is refused with SystemError by special_offset_from_member, typeobject.c:5277-5283, since the members are _Py_T_OBJECT) and runs no finalizer itself; its reads past the block for objects whose Py_SIZE disagrees with the allocation follow from the already-refuted size-attribute paths.

name: structseq_new_impl
reason: newImplC now keeps the two PyDict_GET_SIZE reads apart (size0 at :238, size1 at :255) and makes each dict lookup its own outcome (look i name), with the conversion Py-valued and able to rebind the sizes; NewImplSpecC gives the exact result in source order (conversion error, not-a-dict, the three length messages, MemoryError, the filled object or the unexpected-name TypeError), which an always-failing or length-blind constructor fails; its hypotheses are the honest sizes kept by the conversion (violation refuted as typeobj-structseq-new-impl-in-bounds) and u <= v, the structseq.c:23-24 precondition whose violation at :242 the newtype-nseq-past-fields record describes.

name: structseq_repr
reason: structseqRepr now computes the prealloc in Py_ssize_t with wraparound (-fno-strict-overflow) and lets PyUnicodeWriter_Create fail (ValueError for a negative length, unicode_writer.c:107-111, MemoryError through walloc), and ReprShape states exactly those outcomes before the text, which agrees with the 2**40/2**61/2**62 checks on 3.15.2 since walloc is arbitrary; the remaining scope limit, that later writer growth cannot fail, is acceptable because every deterministic size failure happens at creation and growth only appends text that already exists in memory; item __repr__ failure is mirrored, and repr-labels is a sound refutation (gh-154387 duplicate).

name: structseq_reduce
reason: reduceC mirrors :351-374 (get_real_size, Py_SIZE, the n_unnamed_fields read, PyTuple_FromArray's ordered reads, tp_members[i - u] with decoding before the item) and ReduceSpecC pins the read failure for every type and object and the exact (vals[:v], [(name, vals[i])]) or first decode error on the honest layout, so a reduce that always raises fails it; the u <= v hypothesis is the structseq.c:23-24 precondition and its violation is now on record (typeobj-structseq-reduce-in-bounds-built, reproduced), as is rebinding n_unnamed_fields (typeobj-structseq-reduce-in-bounds).

name: structseq_replace
reason: replaceC now treats each PyDict_PopString as its own outcome (pop i name, so a str-subclass key's __eq__ may raise) and reads PyDict_GET_SIZE after the loop; ReplaceSpecC gives the exact result in source order (positional refusal, unnamed-field refusal, MemoryError, the copy, or each field popped-or-kept with the first decode or pop error and the leftover TypeError), and rebinding the sizes is refuted as typeobj-structseq-replace-in-bounds; the abstract ReplaceSpec no longer claims the row.

name: count_members
reason: countMembers is the walk to the terminator counting the PyStructSequence_UnnamedField pointers; countMembers_eq, and NewTypeOutcomes and NewTypeLayout through the dict and members they state, pin both counts in every build, and it has no failure exit; the NewType refutations run it.

name: initialize_members
reason: initMembersLoop mirrors :545-567 (PyMem_NEW of n - u + 1 entries, skip unnamed, member k at slot i, the sentinel); NewTypeOutcomes (rechecked after 697ae9c) pins the MemoryError when that allocation fails and, when it succeeds on a valid desc without an offset-named field, the build with tp_members = the named fields at their own indices, so an initialize_members that always or never fails is caught.

name: initialize_static_fields
reason: staticBasicsize is :581-582 in Py_ssize_t with no (int) cast, and initType2 stores tp_name, tp_members and that basicsize (the flags at :590 are a stated scope limit and feed no modelled outcome); InitType2Outcomes pins the basicsize it sets on every desc: 32 + 8 * hidden in the built type for 0 <= n_in_sequence <= #fields (matching NewType through StaticTwin), the tp_dictoffset SystemError once it is <= 0 (n_in_sequence >= #fields + 5, typeobject.c:9571-9577), and for 8..24 and the 0 that inherits 32 (:8812-8813) the unchecked path to the over-read at #fields + 1..4, so a wrong formula fails it; that over-read is refuted with a reproducing record as typeobj-structseq-static-twin-all.

name: _PyStructSequence_InitBuiltinWithFlags
reason: The internal-bootstrap reason applies: it is declared extern (no PyAPI_FUNC) in Include/internal/pycore_structseq.h under Py_BUILD_CORE, and its only callers (Python/sysmodule.c, Python/thread.c, Python/errors.c, Objects/longobject.c, Objects/floatobject.c, through _PyStructSequence_InitBuiltin) initialise fixed static descs at interpreter start-up.

name: PyStructSequence_InitType2
reason: initType2 mirrors :688-703 and type_ready's order (ReadyRest before, during and after type_ready_fill_dict, the basicsize rules after them, tp_dict kept on failure at typeobject.c:9665-9667, immortal before type_ready at :9719-9724); InitType2Outcomes now gives the exact (result, state) pair for every refcount, desc, allocator and step outcome, with no size bound since the static basicsize has no cast: the :689 refusal, MemoryError, each ReadyRest step's own exception with the members freed and descriptors as the step left them, the built type or the visible-name decode error for 0 <= n_in_sequence <= #fields, the tp_dictoffset SystemError for >= #fields + 5, the tupleobject.c:40 SystemError for a negative one with the type left ready, and the over-read (after any earlier decode error) for #fields + 1..4; every failure is an exact .exc, so an InitType2 returning -1 with no exception or a different exception on any path fails it; StaticTwin (offset names excluded, refuted as static-twin-valid), static-twin-all and the dangling-descriptor refutation stand, each with a reproducing record.

name: PyStructSequence_InitType
reason: initType is `(void)PyStructSequence_InitType2(type, desc)`: StaticTwin's third conjunct proves, for every refcount, desc, allocator and outcome of the rest, that it returns with no exception exactly when InitType2 succeeds and otherwise with InitType2's exception still set, which is the whole behaviour of the wrapper (a wrapper that cleared the error or reported success differently fails it); it does not depend on the shared-rest issue of the InitType2 row.

name: _PyStructSequence_FiniBuiltin
reason: The internal-bootstrap reason applies: extern in the internal header and called only from the finalization of the same static builtin struct sequence types, after which that interpreter runs no Python code against them.

name: _PyStructSequence_NewType
reason: newType mirrors :753-792 (count, members, the (int)-cast spec.basicsize, FromSpecWithBases's use of it, now with the offset-name scan of typeobject.c:5443-5451 and special_offset_from_member's SystemError in the order :5651-5665 checks them, after the extend and inherit rules and before the basicsize check at :5781, then the dict and __match_args__); NewTypeOutcomes pins every outcome (MemoryError, the rest's error, the offset-name SystemError, the exact type for a valid desc, TypeError for n_in_sequence = #fields + 1..3, SystemError for >= #fields + 5 and for a negative one), so an always-failing NewType fails it, and the two cases its bounds leave out are refuted with a reproducing record (+4 reads past the fields; 2^29 hidden fields wrap tp_basicsize to 32); the tp_flags parameter only reaches spec.flags and is a stated scope limit.

name: PyStructSequence_NewType
reason: The wrapper is newType with tp_flags 0, which the model's flag-free newType is exactly; NewTypeOutcomes (with the offset-name case added in 697ae9c) and the newtype-in-bounds, basicsize-exact and reduce-in-bounds-built refutations all cover it.
